source_refs.page_numbering: DOCX source: footer numbers as rendered (assessment runs p181-p193); section names are given in each citation

subject: math

purpose.text: End-of-module check of Topics A to D (Module 3, ordering and comparing length measurements as numbers, and picture graphs). Four tasks, each scored on a 4-step scale (1 to 4 points). The goal for each child is Step 4.

source_ref.section: Standards Addressed; Evaluating Student Learning Outcomes

parts.label: a
parts.child_text: Look at the graph of the vegetables students like best. Each smiley face is 1 student. How many students like carrots best?
parts.source_text: a. How many students like carrots the best? [picture: pictograph of Broccoli, Peas, Carrots]

parts.label: b
parts.child_text: Look at the graph of the vegetables students like best. How many students like carrots and peas best?
parts.source_text: b. How many students like carrots and peas the best?

parts.label: c
parts.child_text: Look at the graph of the vegetables students like best. How many students answered the survey in all?
parts.source_text: c. How many total students answered the survey?

parts.label: d
parts.child_text: Look at the graph of the vegetables students like best. How many more students like broccoli than peas?
parts.source_text: d. How many more students like broccoli than like peas the best?

parts.label: e
parts.child_text: Look at the graph of the vegetables students like best. How many fewer students like broccoli than carrots?
parts.source_text: e. How many fewer students like broccoli than like carrots the best?

parts.label: stem
parts.child_text: Cesar has a piece of string. He wants to compare his dog's path and his cat's path to the water bowl. The string is a lot longer than the dog's path. The string is a lot shorter than the cat's path. Whose path is shorter, the dog's or the cat's?
parts.source_text: Cesar has a piece of string that he wants to use to compare how far his cat’s bed and his dog’s bed are from their shared water bowl. The string is a lot longer than the dog’s path to the bowl. The string is a lot shorter than the cat’s path to the bowl. Whose path is shorter to the water bowl, the dog’s or the cat’s? Draw a picture to show how you know. [picture: cat bed, dog bed, water bowl]

parts.label: stem
parts.child_text: Look at pictures a, b, c, d and e. Each picture measures a bone. Which pictures show a correct measurement? Say the letters.
parts.source_text: 3. Circle the pictures that show a correct measurement. [picture: a-e, bone measured with centimeter cubes (a, b, c) and paper clips (d, e); one square is a centimeter cube]

parts.label: a
parts.child_text: Pictures b and d show a correct measurement of the bone. Give two reasons why they are correct.
parts.source_text: a. Why did you pick these pictures? Explain your thinking with two reasons.

parts.label: b
parts.child_text: Picture b measures the bone with centimeter cubes. Picture d measures the bone with paper clips. What is the length of the bone in each picture?
parts.source_text: b. What was the length measurement of the bone for each correct picture?

parts.label: c
parts.child_text: The same bone is measured with paper clips two times. One time it is 2 paper clips. The other time it is 3 paper clips. Why are the measurements different?
parts.source_text: c. Why are the measurements for (d) and (e) different?

parts.label: a
parts.child_text: Look at the pictures of the train, the pencil and the lollipop. Each one is measured with centimeter cubes. How many centimeters long is each one?
parts.source_text: 4. Measure the length of the picture of each item with centimeter cubes. a. ____ centimeters ____ centimeters ____ centimeters [picture: train, pencil, lollipop; a centimeter cube]

parts.label: b
parts.child_text: The train is 8 centimeters long. The pencil is 11 centimeters long. The lollipop is 9 centimeters long. Put the three in order from shortest to longest.
parts.source_text: b. Order the train, pencil, and lollipop from shortest to longest.

parts.label: c
parts.child_text: The train is 8 centimeters long. The pencil is 11 centimeters long. The lollipop is 9 centimeters long. Which items are longer than the lollipop?
parts.source_text: c. Which item, or items, is longer than the lollipop?

parts.label: d
parts.child_text: The pencil is 11 centimeters long. The train is 8 centimeters long. How much longer is the pencil than the train?
parts.source_text: d. How much longer is the pencil than the train?

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 2 (Identifies that the dog’s path is shorter)

rubrics.correct: Names pictures b and d (in either order).
rubrics.partial: Names only one of b and d, or names b and d with another picture.
rubrics.incorrect: Names pictures that do not include b and d.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 3 (Identifies (b) and (d) as having the proper measurement)

rubrics.correct: Gives at least two key elements in own words: no gaps, no overlaps, endpoints lined up, same-size length units.
rubrics.partial: Gives one key element, or says the pictures look right without a reason.
rubrics.incorrect: Gives reasons that are not true for measuring.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 3 (Cites at least two key elements to measuring accurately)

rubrics.correct: Says 4 centimeters for picture b and 2 paper clips for picture d.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 3 (2 paper clips and 4 centimeters; units are required)

rubrics.correct: Says the paper clips are different sizes (one kind is longer or smaller), so a different number of them fits along the same bone.
rubrics.partial: Says the measurements are different but does not give the size of the units as the reason, or says only that the paper clips are different.
rubrics.incorrect: Gives a reason that is not true, for example one bone is longer.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 3 (different lengths of units can give different quantities for the same length item)

rubrics.correct: Says train 8, pencil 11 and lollipop 9 centimeters.
rubrics.partial: Gets one or two of the three lengths right.
rubrics.incorrect: None of the three lengths is right.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 4 (train 8 cm, pencil 11 cm, lollipop 9 cm)

accept: the train, the lollipop, the pencil

rubrics.correct: Puts them in the order train, lollipop, pencil.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 4 (Orders the items by length: train, lollipop, pencil)

rubrics.incorrect: Names the train, or names the train and the pencil.
rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 4 (Identifies the pencil as longer than the lollipop)

rubrics.unclear: No answer that can be understood.

source_ref.section: Step 4, Task 4 (the pencil is 3 centimeters longer than the train)

steps.descriptor: Student demonstrates little to no understanding of how to read or interpret the graph.

Student demonstrates some understanding of how many students are represented in the graph in a given category or categories (may be off by one or two) but is unable to solve either of the comparison problems accurately.
Student correctly solves (a), (b), and (c) but solves (d) or (e) incorrectly. OR Student solves the comparison problems (d) and (e) correctly but is unable to correctly solve (a), (b), and/or (c).

Student correctly: Identifies, labels, and solves (a) as 7, (b) as 11, and (c) as 16. Compares the quantities and writes the difference between the two quantities for questions (d) 1 student and (e) 2 students.

full_credit_requirements: Identifies, labels, and solves (a) as 7, (b) as 11, and (c) as 16.
Compares the quantities and writes the difference between the two quantities for questions (d) 1 student and (e) 2 students.

steps.descriptor: Student demonstrates little to no understanding of the comparison.
Student demonstrates some understanding of how the string can be used to compare the two paths (i.e., by using pictures) but provides inaccurate responses.

Student identifies that the dog’s path is shorter but is unable to provide a clear explanation. OR Student incorrectly identifies that the cat’s path is shorter but is able to draw a picture to explain (this may reflect a linguistic interpretation issue).
Student correctly: Identifies that the dog’s path is shorter. Explains how the string could be used to compare the distance from each pet’s bed to the water bowl (transitivity) by drawing pictures.

full_credit_requirements: Identifies that the dog’s path is shorter.
Explains how the string could be used to compare the distance from each pet’s bed to the water bowl (transitivity) by drawing pictures.

steps.descriptor: Student demonstrates little to no understanding of proper measurement techniques or the reasoning behind them.

Student demonstrates some understanding of proper measurement techniques by either selecting or measuring the correct items but cannot explain her thinking clearly and accurately. OR Student demonstrates some understanding of her thinking behind measurement methods but cannot measure or identify measurements accurately.

Student clearly and accurately completes three out of the four following components: Identifies (b) and (d) as having the proper measurement. Cites at least two key elements to measuring accurately (no gaps, no overlaps, attentive to endpoints, same-sized length units) in his own words. Identifies two correct measurements (2 paper clips and 4 centimeters; units are not required). Explains that measuring with different lengths of units (small or large paper clips) can result in different quantities of measurement for the same length item.

Student clearly and accurately: Identifies (b) and (d) as having the proper measurement. Cites at least two key elements to measuring accurately (no gaps, no overlaps, attentive to endpoints, same-sized length units) in his own words. Identifies two correct measurements (2 paper clips and 4 centimeters; units are required). Explains that measuring with different lengths of units (small or large paper clips) can result in different quantities of measurement for the same length item.

full_credit_requirements: Identifies (b) and (d) as having the proper measurement.
Cites at least two key elements to measuring accurately (no gaps, no overlaps, attentive to endpoints, same-sized length units) in his own words.
Identifies two correct measurements (2 paper clips and 4 centimeters; units are required).
Explains that measuring with different lengths of units (small or large paper clips) can result in different quantities of measurement for the same length item.

steps.descriptor: Student demonstrates little to no understanding of how to measure or use the measurement to compare.
Student demonstrates some understanding of how to measure but is unable to manipulate the measurements to order or compare.

Student accurately measures and orders the items by length but is unable to solve either of the comparison problems. OR Student is able to solve the comparison problems correctly but with slight inaccuracy in the measurements (i.e., off by 1 or 2 centimeters, which then impacts the accuracy of (d)).

Student clearly and accurately: Measures the train (8 cm), pencil (11 cm), and lollipop (9 cm). Orders the items by length (train, lollipop, pencil). Identifies the pencil as longer than the lollipop. Solves the comparison problem correctly by identifying the pencil as 3 centimeters longer than the train.

full_credit_requirements: Measures the train (8 cm), pencil (11 cm), and lollipop (9 cm).
Orders the items by length (train, lollipop, pencil).
Identifies the pencil as longer than the lollipop.
Solves the comparison problem correctly by identifying the pencil as 3 centimeters longer than the train.
reference_answers: the pencil is longer than the lollipop
the pencil is 3 centimeters longer than the train

assets_required.why_this_method: A picture graph with exact counts per column. Diffusion cannot count reliably.
assets_required.description: A picture graph titled 'Vegetables That Students Like Best'. Three columns (Broccoli, Peas, Carrots) with small icons at the top. Each smiley-face square in a column is one student. A key shows 1 square = 1 student.
must_show_exactly: Exactly 3 columns: Broccoli, Peas, Carrots (source p181)
Exactly 5 smiley squares in the Broccoli column
Exactly 4 smiley squares in the Peas column
Exactly 7 smiley squares in the Carrots column
16 squares in all
Squares are stacked from the bottom with no gaps
Key: 1 square = 1 student
Axis label: Number of Students
states_or_frames: State 2 (optional): one column highlighted when a question names it
assets_required.interaction: No typed input inside the widget. Child answers in the chat.
assets_required.alt_text: A picture graph showing 5 students like broccoli, 4 like peas and 7 like carrots.
assets_required.review_notes: Counts were taken by looking at the page image and match the printed rubric (7, 11, 16, 1, 2) and the sample work on p190.
assets_required.generation_caption: Clean picture graph with three labeled columns and stacks of smiley-face squares: 5, 4 and 7, plain background. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Five bone pictures with exact unit counts, gaps and endpoints. Anything with exact counts and layout is built by code.
assets_required.description: Five framed pictures a to e. Each shows a bone with a row of units under it: centimeter cubes in a, b, c and paper clips in d and e. Picture b has 4 cubes touching with no gaps and lined up with both ends of the bone. Picture d has 2 paper clips end to end. A key shows one square is a centimeter cube.
must_show_exactly: Exactly 5 pictures labeled a, b, c, d, e (source p183)
Picture a: 3 cubes (labeled 3 centimeters) with gaps between the cubes
Picture b: exactly 4 cubes touching, both bone endpoints matched, labeled 4 centimeters
Picture c: 5 cubes (labeled 5 centimeters); the flaw must be copied from the source picture
Picture d: exactly 2 paper clips end to end, labeled 2 paper clips
Picture e: exactly 3 smaller paper clips, labeled 3 paper clips
The bone in d and e is the same length
assets_required.interaction: No typed input inside the widget. Child answers in the chat.
assets_required.alt_text: Five pictures of a bone measured with cubes or paper clips, labeled a to e.
assets_required.review_notes: Only b and d are known correct (printed Step 4). The exact flaws in a, c and e were not clear in the converted DOCX. A person must copy them from the original pictures.
assets_required.generation_caption: Five framed pictures of a flat cartoon bone with a row of unit squares or paper clips under it, plain background, no extra text. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Three items with exact lengths in centimeter cubes. Diffusion cannot keep lengths exact.
assets_required.description: Pictures of a train, a pencil and a lollipop, each shown with a ruler of centimeter cubes laid along it. The train is 8 cubes long, the pencil 11 cubes, and the lollipop 9 cubes.
must_show_exactly: Exactly 3 items: train, pencil, lollipop (source p184)
Train length is exactly 8 centimeter cubes
Pencil length is exactly 11 centimeter cubes
Lollipop length is exactly 9 centimeter cubes
Cubes touch with no gaps or overlaps and start at each item's endpoint
states_or_frames: State 2: cubes laid along each item
assets_required.interaction: No typed input inside the widget. Child answers in the chat.
assets_required.alt_text: A train, a pencil and a lollipop, each measured along its length with centimeter cubes.
assets_required.review_notes: The lollipop picture was not visible in the converted DOCX. Lengths come from the printed Step 4 (8, 11, 9 cm). A person must check them against the original picture.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat train, pencil and lollipop with a row of square cubes laid end to end under each, train 8, pencil 11, lollipop 9, plain background. [Build by code]

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).

Task 2 has no part letters, so it is one stem part. The facts about the string are printed, so it is not image-dependent. The picture (cat bed, dog bed, bowl) is not used. The printed drawing is not judged.
Explain parts: a drawn explanation or written work on paper is not judged. The open rubrics follow the printed Step 4 bullets.

Child text repeats facts so each part stands alone: ai_3a says b and d are correct; ai_3c says it is the same bone with 2 and 3 paper clips (from the labels and the printed rubric). Check this wording.
The printed Step 4 needs units (2 paper clips, 4 centimeters). Step 3 does not. The key accepts bare numbers too, so a unit check must happen in scoring.
Child text includes the lengths 8, 11 and 9 centimeters (from the printed Step 4) so each part stands alone. Check this wording.
Printed in the rubric table (source): all rubrics. The parts are derived or adapted. Accepted word forms in r_ai_4b are mine. Recompute by hand: 5+4+7=16, 7+4=11, 5-4=1, 7-5=2, 11-8=3.
The 4-step table was read from the Word table cells and checked against the page images (pages 187 to 189). The 4-step score cannot be fully computed from Tutor answers: drawings are not judged.
Pages 190 to 192 are sample work (Maria) and were not converted into items. They were used only to cross-check answers. Page 193 is blank.
